[MUQATIL:9:75-79/r5] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | The secret and private conversation refers to the plot agreed upon by the people of the Aqaba to kill the Prophet.
[TAB-FULL:v11p587/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | The hypocrites secretly disbelieve in God and His Messenger while publicly showing belief to believers; God knows their hidden disbelief.

[TAB-FULL:v11p587/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | God is the Knower of all that is hidden from created beings' hearing, sight, and senses and remains concealed in their hearts.
[TAB-FULL:v11p587/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Awareness of God's knowledge should stop hypocrites from deceiving His allies through hypocrisy and lies or showing outwardly what contradicts their inward belief.
[IBNABIHATIM:v6p1849#2/r1] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · الضحاك | reports | Al-Dahhak says God knows what is more hidden than a secret, including what a person has not yet done but will do.
[SULAMI:v1p282#4/r1] SULAMI, d. 412 · author | holds | The secret is what only the Knower of secrets can see, while private conversation is what the recording angels can see.
[QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r20] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | God warns them through His knowledge as He warns them elsewhere through His acts.
[QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r21] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Their secret is what no one besides God can see.
[QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r22] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Their private conversation is what they say confidentially to one another; the term may also include thoughts surveyed by their own souls.
[JISHUMI:v1p448/r1] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The passage exposes and warns against the hypocrites’ obstinate rejection: they knew the truth but abandoned it, and its disclosure of their secrets is a sign of the Prophet’s miracle.
[JISHUMI:v1p448/r10] JISHUMI, d. 494 · أبو علي | reports | Abū ʿAlī says they should know that the God they already acknowledge knows their secrets and what they make public, showing that they recognized God.
[JISHUMI:v1p448/r3] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Iʿlān means making something manifest or perceptible; it is the opposite of concealment, isrār.
[JISHUMI:v1p448/r6] JISHUMI, d. 494 · الحسن وقتادة وجماعة | reports | Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, and others say God knows their concealed rejection of Muhammad and their public profession to believers that they have faith.
[JISHUMI:v1p448/r7] JISHUMI, d. 494 · أبو علي وأبو مسلم | reports | Abū ʿAlī and Abū Muslim take the words generally: God knows everything people hide and make public.
[JISHUMI:v1p448/r8] JISHUMI, d. 494 · unspecified | reports | Another explanation asks whether they do not know that their deceptions cannot fool one who knows private and public matters.
[JISHUMI:v1p448/r9] JISHUMI, d. 494 · أبو مسلم | reports | Abū Muslim says they should have known from the signs and proofs God established that He knows their private and public affairs.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p78#2/r1] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | Their secret is what they conceal in their hearts, and their private conversations are what they discuss among themselves.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p78#2/r2] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | God knows all unseen things.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p62#2/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The opening of this verse is connected to the interpretation that the previous pact was made by intention rather than speech.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p62#2/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الجمهور | reports | The majority read يعلموا with yāʾ, in the third person.

[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p62#2/r7] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The verse rebukes their secret plotting to disparage Islam and their private coordination against the Prophet, his community, and his law; its warning applies to all hypocrites.

[TABRISI:9:75-78/r7] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Najwa is secret speech; its related verbs include nājā, tanājā, and intajā, and its plural is anjiya. The root suggests distance from others, or alternatively a raised place beyond a flood's reach where speech is private.
[TABRISI:9:77-78/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The question rebukes the hypocrites and means that they ought to know God is aware of what they conceal and privately discuss.
[TABRISI:9:77-78/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | “Their secret” is what they hide within themselves, and “their private conversation” is what they say confidentially among themselves.
[TABRISI:9:77-78/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The plural “unseen things” covers what is absent from bodies and human perception, whether existent or nonexistent, in every respect it can be known; the form is intensive.

[RAZI-FULL:v16p114/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | rejects | Razi rejects that inference: where separate evidence excludes vision in a particular use of meeting, it does not require excluding vision from every other use.
[RAZI-FULL:v16p114/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Secret is what breasts conceal; najwā is private discussion among people, from najwa, a secluded elevation or place, since interlocutors exclude others; Razi links 19:52, 12:80, 58:9, and 58:12. | mentions 19:52, 12:80, 58:9, 58:12
[RAZI-FULL:v16p115/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The warning is that hypocrites dare to conspire despite knowing God sees their hidden and whispered conduct as clearly as the public, and punishes it likewise.
[RAZI-FULL:v16p115/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | ʿAllām intensifies ʿālim; the unseen is what creatures cannot perceive, and God’s essence entails knowledge of every thing, including inner thoughts, so nothing can be hidden from Him.
[RAZI-FULL:v16p115/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Razi compares this divine title with Jesus’ words in 5:116. | mentions 5:116
[RAZI-FULL:v16p115/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Calling God ʿallāma is improper because the form suggests effortful learning, and effort is impossible for God.

[QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The question is a rebuke: God knows their secrets and private counsels, so He will requite them.
[QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · كثير من التابعين والأئمة | reports | Many Successors and imams adopted the broad interpretation of the hypocrisy traits discussed in the preceding report.
[QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · طائفة | reports | One group says the traits designate a person only when they predominate in his character.

[QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن العربي | reports | Ibn al-Arabi says even when sins predominate, they do not make someone an unbeliever unless they affect his belief.
[QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · علماؤنا | reports | The scholars argue that Joseph’s brothers broke a pledge, lied to their father, and betrayed Joseph, yet were not hypocrites.
[QURTUBI-FULL:9:78/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · عطاء بن أبي رباح | reports | ʿAta says Joseph’s brothers committed these traits without being hypocrites, since they were prophets.

item.text: I’ve read all 96 notes. Several sources connect the wording to the earlier covenant, while others read it as a warning to hypocrites generally. I’m keeping those views distinct and placing the reading variants with their stated audiences.
